title: zirc
description: Generated from zirc-proto and zirc-core by `bazel run //crates/zirc-core:generated_types`. Don't edit: change the Rust types and generate this again.

oneOf.description:
The organisation's agents channel, [`zirc_proto::AGENTS_CHANNEL`], which every
repository's sessions share, the post saying its repository. Said as `default`, which a
zircd from before 20 Nov 2026, still running under a newer CLI, takes too (as its
agents room); what such a CLI sends for the channels repositories had (`repo`,
`branch`) goes here too.
oneOf.title: DefaultTarget

oneOf.description: The organisation's channel, `#general`.
oneOf.title: OrgTarget

oneOf.description: The organisation's channel for a topic, which must have been joined.
oneOf.title: TopicTarget

Target.description: Which channel a post goes to.

oneOf.description: Fine: what a state is when nobody has said otherwise.
Worth knowing before relying on it, such as a flaky check.
Broken: work that relies on it will fail until it's fixed.

role.description: The role it's for, such as `fixer`.

key.description: What makes it the same as an earlier one: a warning's line, a test, a workload.

summary.description: What it says, in a line; the key when its sender says nothing more.

link.description: Where to read more, such as the build's log.

details.description: More of what's known, such as a container's exit code and restarts.

build.description: The CI build it was seen in.

tool.description: The tool that posted it to the role's address ([`crate::inbound`]), when one did.

reference.description: What the tool calls it, as people know it there: `#412`, `ENG-12`.

RoleReport.description: A report to a role: what an [`Event::Custom`] of [`KIND`] carries.

oneOf.description:
A new warning or deprecation notice in CI's logs: its key is the warning's line, as
`ops/lib.sh`'s `warnings` prints it.
A test that failed, then passed when run again: its key is the test.

A container that restarted, or a tenant's server that stays not ready: its key is
the workload, `<namespace>/<name>`.

An error a tool such as Sentry caught ([`crate::inbound`]): its key is the tool's
issue.
A new issue in a tracker, GitHub's or Linear's: its key is the issue.
An incident, `PagerDuty`'s: its key is the incident.

Subject.description:
What a report is about. Kinds are added here; a sidecar older than a kind doesn't read its
reports, as it couldn't say what they are.

oneOf.description: Sentry: its issue and error alerts.
GitHub: a repository's `issues` events.
Linear: its Issue webhooks.
`PagerDuty`: its v3 incident webhooks.
Any other tool: what it posts arrives as a message to the role.

Tool.description: A tool that posts to a role's address.

end.description:
How it ended: done or baselined by the holder, resolved by the tool that reported it
(said by the role's nick), never landed, which only CI says.

Closing.description:
The holder says an item is done or baselined: what an [`Event::Custom`] of
[`CLOSED_KIND`] carries.

oneOf.description: A landing that names it passed.
Its holder said it's done.

Its holder added it to the baseline: it can't be fixed here, as a dependency's own
warning.
The tool that reported it said it's resolved there, as Sentry does of an issue.
❓ 🤔 👀: tell me more.

🤷: the session's call, to go ahead on its own judgement. Never an answer to a request
that can't be undone, which a person decides.
No one: queries are dropped.

The owner's own: this machine's other sessions, the owner, and the owner's other
machines, told by the account the server says sent the query.
Anyone signed in to an account on the server. [`ANYONE_WARNING`] says why it's risky.

Queries.description: Who may query this machine's agents.

repo.description:
The repository it's in, as [`crate::project::Project::scope`] names it, such as
`#monorepo`: any repository's when absent.

level.description:
How it stands as the session asks: a state said at any other level wakes it. Absent
when it was never said, so the first said wakes it.

StateWait.description:
A state a session waits on changing ([`Request::WaitFor`]), such as `master` while it's
broken ([`zirc_proto::state`]).

nick.description: The nick on its server, while connected.

problem.description: Why zircd isn't connecting to it, when it's stopped trying.

window_minutes.description: The window wakes are counted over, in minutes.

per_session.description: The most wakes of one session in the window.

machine.description: The most wakes of all this machine's sessions in the window.

wakes.description: The wakes let through in the window.

paused_machine.description: Whether no session wakes, the machine's limit being reached.

paused_sessions.description: The sessions that don't wake, each having reached its own limit.

held.description: How many wakes were held since it last paused any.

top.description: What woke sessions most in the window, most first, as `mention from cc-1 ×5`.

BreakerState.description:
zircd's circuit breaker on wakes: how many it let through lately, its limits, and whether
it's holding them, past a limit, as notes for each session's next wake.

connected.description: Whether the IRC connection is up.

nick.description: The nick on the server, while connected.

problem.description:
Why zircd isn't connecting, when it's stopped trying until something changes, such
as [`REVOKED`].

watching.description:
The sessions with a watch running, sorted, `None` for a watch without one: what
`zirc watch` started, and whether it's still there.

protocol.description:
The socket protocol zircd speaks, [`PROTOCOL`]; 0 from a zircd that predates
versions, which speaks version 1.

version.description: zircd's version. zircds from before 0.1.11 don't say.

orgs.description:
Each organisation's connection, when this machine is signed in to several: the
fields above are then the first's.

breaker.description: The circuit breaker on wakes, from a zircd that has one.

busy_ms.description:
The longest zircd was busy with one thing in the last minute or two, in milliseconds:
how long a command can have waited for it. From a zircd that measures it.

path.description: The root of its working tree.

scope.description:
How lines about it, hints and shared states name it
([`crate::project::Project::scope`]), `#<name>`: the channel its work went to before
20 Nov 2026. Compare a line's [`Delivery::scope`].

sessions.description: Every session added with it, the last one added last.

org.description:
The organisation it belongs to, whose server alone hears about it. zircds from
before several organisations don't say.

shared.description:
Sessions registered here in the last day that another worktree, still there, had
registered: two sessions under one name, which `zirc` warns of (decided 8 Nov
2026: a warning, never a refusal). zircds from before it don't say.

RepoSession.description: A session working in a watched repository.

at.description: When, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

Shared.description: A session one worktree registered that another, still there, had registered before it.

org.description: The organisation whose channel it is, when this machine is signed in to several.

members.description: Each machine with uncommitted changes, by nick.

claims.description: What sessions have said they're taking on, oldest first.

intents.description: What sessions have said they're about to touch, and haven't finished or let expire.

landings.description: The latest pushes to the default branch, newest first.

built.description: What each worktree's work is built on and changes, for those whose machines say.

ChannelPresence.description: The working sets in one channel.

worktree.description: For this machine, which of its worktrees.

name.description:
The name of the worktree's directory, when known: a better label than a branch
named by a tool, such as `mg-branch-39`.

branch.description: The branch the paths are changed on, when known.

session.description: The session working there, when known.

session_name.description: What that session's called, when it says ([`Message::name`]).

session_tool.description: The agent tool that session runs in, when it says ([`Message::tool`]).

session_avatar.description: The picture that session goes by, when it says ([`Message::avatar`]).

paths.description: The paths it has uncommitted changes in, sorted.

Member.description:
One worktree's working set in a channel, or a whole machine's when it doesn't say which
worktree its paths are in, as zircds before 0.2 don't.

branch.description: The branch checked out, unless HEAD is detached.

Worktree.description: A working tree on this machine, and the branch checked out in it.

session_name.description: What that session's called, when it says ([`Message::name`]).

session_tool.description: The agent tool that session runs in, when it says ([`Message::tool`]).

session_avatar.description: The picture that session goes by, when it says ([`Message::avatar`]).

task.description: What it's taking on, as it said it.

since.description: When it said so, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

Claim.description:
What a session said it's taking on, with `zirc post "taking: …"`, until it posts
`done: …` or `dropped: …` or leaves.

session_name.description: What that session's called, when it says ([`Message::name`]).

session_tool.description: The agent tool that session runs in, when it says ([`Message::tool`]).

session_avatar.description: The picture that session goes by, when it says ([`Message::avatar`]).

summary.description: What it's about to do, as it said it.

paths.description: The paths or directories it expects to touch.

expires.description: When it ends, in seconds since the Unix epoch, if it does on its own.

Intent.description:
What a session said it's about to touch, with `zirc intend`, until it expires, the
session posts `done: …` or `dropped: …`, or its machine leaves.

nick.description: The nick of the machine that pushed.

branch.description: The branch pushed, the default one.

subjects.description: The subjects of the commits it pushed, oldest first.

paths.description: The paths they changed, when the push said.

at.description: When it was heard, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

Landing.description: A push to a repository's default branch: work that's landed.

session.description: The session working there, when known.

branch.description: The branch checked out there, when known.

base.description:
The commit of the default branch its work is built on, by the start of its id
([`zirc_proto::BASE_DIGITS`] digits).

changed.description: The paths its work changes since `base`, committed or not, sorted.

Built.description:
What a worktree's work is built on and all it changes, as its machine says: enough to
tell, of something that landed, whether the work is behind it and depends on it.

tip.description: Its head as the session built on it: what a rebase leaves behind.

moved.description: Its head since, when a push moved it from `tip`.

dropped.description:
Whether it was deleted from origin without landing: dropped, not to be landed in its
place.

Stack.description: A branch a session's branch is stacked on ([`Request::Stack`]).

channel.description: The channel it was sent to.

from.description: The nick it came from: the sending machine, or the person.

id.description:
The server's id for it (`IRCv3`'s `msgid`), which [`Request::Trim`] names. This
machine's own posts, which the server doesn't echo back, come without one: find
theirs with [`Request::Read`].

time.description: When the server says it was sent, in RFC 3339, when it says.

why.description: Why it concerns the watching session, if it does.

reply.description: The id of the message it replies to (`IRCv3`'s `+draft/reply`), if it's a reply.

org.description:
The organisation whose server it came from, while watching on a machine signed in
to several.

account.description: The account the server says sent it (`account-tag`), when it says.

hosted_by.description:
Whose machine the server says sent it, by its host (`machine/<owner>`,
[`crate::agents::host_owner`]): None for a person.

client_of.description:
Whose own client the server says sent it, by its host (`client/<person>`,
[`zirc_proto::names::client_host`]): a person signed in themself under another name,
as in an IRC client, whose word it is as their own account's is. None otherwise.

decided.description:
For a decision ([`zirc_proto::decision`]): how sure it is the decider's own word, as
this machine can tell from [`Delivery::account`].

fit.description:
For another session's intent ([`Why::Intent`]): how it meets the watching session's
work, file by file, as zircd can tell.

sealed.description:
Its sealed parts, the `+zirc.dev/sealed` tag's value ([`zirc_proto::sealed`]), when
it has some: each is a `[sealed]` in its text, which `zirc unseal` opens.

own_branch.description:
For CI's line on a build ([`Why::Awaited`]): whether it's of a branch the watching
session pushed, which zircd waits on for it, rather than one it said it waits on.

Delivery.description:
A message someone sent to a channel: a zirc one, or plain text a person typed in an IRC
client, which arrives as a text event with an empty session.

v.description: The format version, [`VERSION`] when written by this crate.

session.description:
The agent session or person on the sending machine. The machine itself is the
IRC nick the message arrives from.

app.description:
For one of zirc's own integrations, the short name apps show for it in place of a
generic app badge, such as `deploy`: see [`app_label`]. Without it, apps show its
session's.

name.description:
What people call its session, such as `zirc-chat` or `docs-site`, which apps show
in place of an id like `cc-598aa1`: see [`session_name`]. Without it, they show the
session.

tool.description:
The agent tool its session runs in, such as `claude-code` or `codex`, so apps can
show its icon: see [`session_tool`]. Without it, the session is a person's or
runs in a tool zirc doesn't know.

avatar.description:
The picture its session picked from [`AGENT_AVATARS`], by id, such as `rocket`, which
apps show in place of the tool's icon. Without it, they show the tool's.

everyone.description:
Whether it's for every session hearing it, as `zirc post --everyone` says: an agent's
broadcast. Never its text: `@everyone` written in it, as in a quote or a code block,
is only text.

level.description:
What it asks of whoever reads it, as its sender says: see [`Level`]. Without it, the
level its kind and data say ([`Message::level`]).

task.description:
The task its session is on, so a task's posts, intents, commits and landing can be
told apart from the rest: the id zircd gives a session when it posts `taking:`
([`task_id`]), kept until it posts `done:` or `dropped:` ([`says_finished`]). Only
an id, never what the task is.

repo.description:
The repository it's about, by name as zirc spells it (`monorepo` for
`git@github.com:zircd/monorepo.git`): every repository's sessions and CI speak in the
organisation's one [`AGENTS_CHANNEL`], so a reader tells them apart by this. Apps show
it only where the organisation has more than one. Without it, it's about none, as a
person's line.

summary.description: One line, as a person would say it.

paths.description: Paths or directories it expects to touch, relative to the repository root.

expires.description:
When it ends unless renewed, in seconds since the Unix epoch, by the sender's
clock. One without lasts until its session is done.

lasts.description:
How many seconds it lasts from when it was sent: from the message's server time,
which works for replayed messages and other clocks alike. Readers prefer it to
`expires`, which stays for readers that predate it.

oneOf.description:
What a session is about to work on, sent before it starts editing so that others
changing the same paths hear of it while it's cheap to avoid. A session's intent
replaces its previous one, and ends when it expires or the session posts `done:` or
`dropped:`.
oneOf.title: IntentEvent

continued.description: Whether this adds to the previous message's paths rather than replacing them.

worktree.description: The name of the worktree's directory the paths are in; never its full path.

branch.description: The branch checked out in that worktree, unless its HEAD is detached.

part.description:
Which part of the set this is and how many there are, counting from 1, or
[`ALONE`] for one worktree's set said alone.

base.description:
The commit the worktree's work is built on: the newest commit of the remote's
default branch that it has, by the first [`BASE_DIGITS`] digits of its id, as a
line has little room. With it, anyone who knows what landed since can tell
whether the work is behind a landing. Left out without a remote default branch,
where it doesn't fit, and by machines that predate it.

committed.description:
The paths the worktree's own commits since `base` change, beyond `paths`: with
`paths`, all its work changes. A worktree with commits of its own and nothing
uncommitted is said with these alone, which readers that predate them take as a
worktree with no changes.

oneOf.description:
Every path a machine has uncommitted changes in, relative to the repository root,
sent whenever the set changes and when someone joins. A set too long for one line is
split: the first part replaces what the receiver knew, and the parts after it are
marked `continued` and add to it.

A machine with several worktrees sends one part per worktree with changes, each
naming its worktree and branch, and the message's session is the one working there.
A reader that ignores `worktree` and `branch` still gets the machine's whole set. A
machine whose worktrees are all clean sends one part with no paths.

Each part also says which it is of how many, so a reader that gets only some of
them, as a history replay cut short can give it, can tell and keep what it had.

Between whole sets, a machine says a worktree's changed set alone, numbered [`ALONE`]:
it replaces that worktree's set and no other.
oneOf.title: WorkingEvent

branch.description: The branch it was made on.

subject.description: The first line of its message.

paths.description:
The paths it changed, relative to the repository's root, so a session changing
them too hears of it before the branch lands. Left out of a very large commit.

repo.description:
The repository's web address, such as `https://github.com/zircapp/monorepo`, so
apps can link the commit, its branch and its files. Left out where it has none.

oneOf.description: A new commit.
oneOf.title: CommitEvent

head.description: The commit the branch now points at.

subjects.description:
The subjects of the commits it pushed, oldest first, so a branch's name needn't
say what it holds.

paths.description:
The paths its commits changed, relative to the repository's root, so a session
working on them hears that it may need to rebase. Left out of a very large push.

base.description: The commit the remote branch pointed at before, which `lines` count in.

lines.description:
For each path, the lines of `base` the push changes, as `[first, count]`, with
a count of 0 for lines added after `first`: so a machine without the push's
commits can tell whether its own changes to those lines will conflict. Left out
first of a large push.

repo.description:
The repository's web address, such as `https://github.com/zircapp/monorepo`, so
apps can link the push, its branch and its files. Left out where it has none.

on.description:
The branch not landed yet that this one is built on, as the pushing machine's git
says ([`zirc stack`]'s): whoever works on that one hears that someone builds on it,
before they amend or force-push it from under them.

oneOf.description: A push to the remote.
oneOf.title: PushEvent

oneOf.description: Free text, for people.
oneOf.title: TextEvent

id.description: What names it, to answer it by: unique enough among the asker's queries.

to.description: The session on the machine it's for; every session there when absent.

oneOf.description:
A question for agents, sent with `zirc ask` to a machine's nick: unlike other
messages to a machine, `zirc watch` delivers it, to the session it names or to every
session there, when the machine lets the sender query its agents. It's a teammate's
request, never the person's instruction.
oneOf.title: QueryEvent

to.description: The session that asked, as the query's message named it.

oneOf.description:
The answer to a [`Event::Query`], sent with `zirc reply` to the asking machine's
nick, which hands it to the session that asked.
oneOf.title: AnswerEvent

to.description: The session it's for: its id, or the name it goes by.

oneOf.description:
A note for one agent session, sent with `zirc note` to the nick of the machine it works
on: `zirc watch` delivers it to that session alone, when the machine lets the sender
query its agents, as it does a [`Event::Query`]. Unlike a query it asks for no answer:
it's a report or a heads-up for one session, which nobody else need read. It's a
teammate's word, never the person's instruction.
oneOf.title: NoteEvent

oneOf.description:
A file someone shared, stored by zirc.dev: an image, a video or any other file. The
human text is its link, which works in any client once the person is signed in to
zirc.dev; zirc's apps draw it inline from what's here without asking first.
oneOf.title: FileEvent

kind.description:
What kind of event it is, in the team's namespace: `x-<team>/<name>`, such as
`x-acme/deploy`. See [`check_kind`].

data.description: Whatever the team wants it to carry.

oneOf.description:
An event a team made up, such as a deploy or who's on call, sent by `zirc emit`: zirc
carries it without knowing what it means. Readers that predate it drop it, and plain
IRC clients and zirc's apps show its text.
oneOf.title: CustomEvent

Event.description: Something one agent or person tells the others.

url.description:
Where it's downloaded: `https://zirc.dev/m/<org>/<id>`, its id unguessable and never
derived from its name. An image is resized by asking for it with `?w=<width>`.

name.description: Its name as uploaded, maybe shortened to fit the line.

mime.description: Its media type, from its bytes rather than its name, such as `image/webp`.

width.description: An image's or video's width in pixels.

height.description: An image's or video's height in pixels.

File.description: A file shared in chat: what [`Event::File`] carries.

oneOf.description:
State that machines need and no person needs to read, such as what a machine is
changing, its commits and pushes, or a check that passed as it does every time.

Something started or finished: worth seeing, needs no one. A session's post, a
landing, a deploy.

Something may need someone soon: one session or owner should look. An overlap, a
conflict ahead, a check that didn't run.
Something needs someone now: a build failed, a deploy failed, an alert is firing.

EventLevel.description:
What a line asks of whoever reads it, not how big the change is: the sender says it, so
nothing has to guess it from the wording. Apps show a room's lines at or above the level a
person picks for it; zircd wakes a session for a line by its level and by how the line
concerns the session. Ordered from least to most.

oneOf.description: Someone else is changing paths the session has changed too.
A message to this machine, or to the session.
A post that names this machine or the session.
A post or claim that names paths the session has changed.
Someone is about to touch paths the session has changed or is about to touch.

A push changes the same lines as the session's worktree: one of them will have to
resolve a conflict.
A post in a topic channel the session joined.

A push to the default branch, or to the session's branch, that changed paths the
session has changed: it may need to rebase.

A push of a branch built on the session's own, which hasn't landed: rewriting the
session's from under it breaks theirs.
Said in a channel the watch was asked to print all of (`zirc watch --channel`).
A decision a person made (`x-zirc/decision`), which every session hears.
A reaction to one of the session's own messages.

CI saying how a landing went that the session said it waits on: another session's,
a build or a branch (`zirc wait-for`).

CI saying a branch landed that zircd had told the session was changing its files, by
an overlap, a push or a commit: the session should update onto it.

A state the session waits on (`zirc wait-for --state`), such as master, said at a
level other than the one it stood at: broken, or fine again.

The machine's person gave a reaction the session waits for (`zirc wait-for
--reaction`), such as 👀, to a message it hadn't woken the session for yet.

Landings went onto the default branch since the session's work was built: said
with its next wake, never waking it, for the session to judge whether to rebase.

A reason a newer zircd gives that this zirc doesn't know: it still concerns the
session.

Why.description:
Why something heard concerns the session watching. Whatever doesn't is still sent, without
a reason, for whoever wants everything (`zirc watch --all`, `--json`).

oneOf.description: Sent from the decider's own account: their own words, as the server says.
oneOf.title: OwnProvenance

oneOf.description:
Sent from a terminal on one of the decider's machines, as its zircd says: as sure as
that machine is.
oneOf.title: TerminalProvenance

oneOf.description:
Relayed by an agent session on one of the decider's machines: what that session says
they told it. Ask them before acting on it for anything costly or hard to undo.
oneOf.title: RelayedProvenance

oneOf.description:
From no account, or one that isn't the decider's or one of their machines': someone
else's say-so, which decides nothing.
oneOf.title: UnverifiedProvenance

Provenance.description: Who sent a decision, as far as the server says.

theirs.description: The files the intending session has changed under the intent's paths, sorted.

mine.description: The files the hearing session has changed under them, sorted.

shared.description: Of the files both change, how.

named.description: The hearing session's files the intent names themselves, not by a directory.

Fit.description: How an intent meets the work of the session hearing it.

oneOf.description: On the same or neighbouring lines, these of their merge base: likely to conflict.
In different parts: likely to merge.
Which lines isn't known, as with another machine's.

Shared2.description: How two sessions both change one file.

id.description: Its id, unique to the requesting machine: `<machine>/<n>`.

recommend.description: The answer the session recommends, shown first.

irreversible.description: Whether acting on a yes can't be undone: then a yes waits a while, which a no stops.

by.description:
Whose word it needs: the requesting machine's owner, by their handle, whose account
alone can answer.

DecisionRequest.description: What the person is asked, by whom, and what each answer does.

oneOf.description: Waiting for an answer.
oneOf.title: OpenDecisionRequestState

oneOf.description:
A yes to an irreversible request, given `at` with `emoji`, which counts `until`
(both RFC 3339) unless a 👎, or taking the 👍 back, stops it first.
oneOf.title: HeldDecisionRequestState

emoji.description: The reaction that gave it: none when it was taken as recommended.

recommended.description:
Whether nobody gave it: the session's recommendation, taken at once as the
person's machine is set to ([`Request::recommend`]). Their reaction on the
request still says otherwise, whenever it comes.

oneOf.description: Answered, `at` (RFC 3339), with `emoji`.
oneOf.title: AnsweredDecisionRequestState

why.description: Why, in a few words, as the card says: [`Withdrawal::said`].

oneOf.description: Taken back unanswered, `at` (RFC 3339): no answer is needed any more, and none counts.
oneOf.title: WithdrawnDecisionRequestState

oneOf.description: Its session took it back (`zirc request --withdraw`).
Its session finished, or dropped, the task it asked for.

Its session ended, or has been away as long as its row stays listed
([`crate::session::AWAY_FOLD_SECS`]).

request.description: The request, as it now stands.

by.description: Who gave it: the owner's account.

msgid.description: The id of the request's message.

org.description:
The organisation whose server it came from, while watching on a machine signed in
to several.

why.description: Why it concerns the watching session: the session asked.

Answered.description:
This machine's owner's answer to a request ([`zirc_proto::request`]): a reaction the
server said their own account gave, on the request's own message, while it was open.

from.description: Who: the nick it came from, a person's or a machine's. `None` for CI and zirc.

session.description: The agent session on [`Self::from`] it came from.

channel.description:
The channel the line that woke it was said in, as it's called on the server; `None`
for what was sent to it directly.

line.description: That line's id on the server, for an app to add its words where its reader has it.

build.description: For CI's line: the build's number.

state.description:
For CI's line, how it stands ([`crate::card::State`], as [`crate::ci::Data::state`]

level.description: For how something the team shares stands, its level.

branch.description: The branch it's about: the one CI built or that landed, or the state's name.

landing.description:
For CI's line, whether it's a landing's ([`crate::ci::LANDING_KIND`]): one that

wake.description: The wake's id ([`crate::activity::Wake::id`]), which joins the line to its record.

role.description:
The role ([`crate::roles`]) the session was woken as, when it was: its line ends
with it, `Woke: master is broken (fixer)`.

report.description:
For a report: the item it opened ([`crate::role_report::OpenItem::id`]) and what was
reported, which its line says, as CI's build is.

excerpt.description:
For a post from a tool zirc doesn't know, how what it sent begins
([`EXCERPT_MAX`] characters), which its line says.

Woke.description: A session's watch woke: what an [`Event::Custom`] of [`KIND`] carries, from the session.

Done, and it didn't.

events.description: How many times it's been reported so far, for a tool's: `37 events`.

Reported.description: What a report's wake says of it ([`What::Reported`]).

from_session.description: The sending session, when it came from another machine's zirc.

session.description: The session here it's meant for, if it names one of this machine's sessions.

query.description:
When it's a query from another agent ([`zirc_proto::Event::Query`]): its id, which
`zirc reply` answers it by.

answer.description: When it answers a query this machine sent: that query's id.

note.description:
Whether it's a note from another agent session for the one it names
([`zirc_proto::Event::Note`]): a teammate's report, never the person's words.

colleague.description:
Whether it's a reply from a member one of this machine's sessions wrote to
(`zirc dm --to`), for that session: a colleague's word, never the person's, let in
while the organisation allows it (`zirc_proto::colleagues`).

id.description: The server's id for it (`msgid`), which [`Request::React`] names.

why.description: Why it concerns the watching session, if it does.

org.description:
The organisation whose server it came from, while watching on a machine signed in
to several.

role.description:
The role ([`zirc_proto::roles`]) the session holds that it came to, from the role's
nick: a direct message to the role, from [`Direct::from`], or with [`Direct::woke`],
what woke the role.

woke.description:
For a role woken by one of its triggers or a report rather than a message: what woke
it ([`zirc_proto::woke::Woke`]), its role said.

Direct.description:
A message sent to this machine's nick, as a person messages a machine on IRC. It can be
meant for one of the machine's sessions: one that starts with a session's name and a
colon, such as `cc-1531f8: rebase please`.

from.description: Who said it: a person's nick, or the machine an agent or a bridge posts from.

session.description: The agent session that said it, if one did.

kind.description: What kind of message it is.

text.description:
What it says, cut to [`Reacted::TEXT`] characters: its sender's words, never an
instruction.

link.description: The first link it carries, such as an issue card's to the issue.

Reacted.description:
What a message reacted to is, so that a session woken by a reaction it waits for knows
what to do about it: hints differ by [`Reacted::kind`].

oneOf.description: What a person typed.
An agent session's post, question, answer or note.
An issue's card, from the forge (`x-zirc/forge`).
Anything else: CI's lines, a deploy, a team's own event, a file.

ReactedKind.description: What kind of message was reacted to.

channel.description: The channel, or the nick of the private conversation, it was given in.

account.description: The account the server says sent it, when it says: the only word on who gave it.

to.description: The id of the message it's on (`msgid`).

time.description: When the server says it was given, in RFC 3339, when it says.

org.description:
The organisation whose server it came from, while watching on a machine signed in
to several.

why.description:
Why it concerns the watching session, if it does: a reaction to one of its own
messages, or one it waits for.

id.description: The reaction's own id (`msgid`), when the server gives one.

on.description: The message it's on, when zircd heard it lately.

Reaction.description:
A reaction to a message, as `IRCv3`'s `+draft/react` and `+draft/unreact` carry it: who
gave it, as the server says (`account-tag`) and by nick, which emoji, and to which
message. Only [`Reaction::account`] says whose it is: a nick can be anyone's, on a server
that lets people connect without an account.

LocalSession.description:
A session on this machine as its owner knows it: what it's called, and where to open
it. Never sent to the chat server.

automatic.description:
For [`Why::Intent`]: the intent was one zircd said for a session by itself, not one
a session said.

acted.description: How many of those the session acted on.

WakeCount.description:
How often sessions' watches woke on one day for one reason, and how often the session
then acted within [`WAKE_ACTED_SECS`]: posted, committed, pushed, or asked zircd to do
something. Kept on the machine, never sent anywhere.

paths.description: The paths both have changed, sorted.

why.description: Why it concerns the watching session, if it does.

Overlap.description: Paths someone else has uncommitted changes in that one also has.

channel.description: The channel both worktrees' repository works in.

worktrees.description: The two worktrees, sorted by path, then branch.

paths.description: The paths both have changed, sorted.

same_lines.description:
Of those, the ones both change on the same or neighbouring lines, with those lines
of their merge base: likely to conflict.

apart.description: Of those, the ones both change in different parts: likely to merge.

why.description: Why it concerns the watching session, if it does.

LocalOverlap.description:
Paths two worktrees on this machine both have uncommitted changes in: two sessions
stepping on each other.

channel.description: The channel the push was announced in.

nick.description: The nick of the machine that pushed.

worktree.description: The worktree whose changes it clashes with.

same_lines.description:
The paths both change on the same or neighbouring lines, with those lines of their
merge base.

why.description: Why it concerns the watching session, if it does.

Conflict.description:
A push of someone else's changing the same lines as a worktree on this machine: what
will conflict when one is merged with the other.

holder.description:
Who holds it, if anyone does: the first of [`Lease::holders`], for readers from
before a lease had [`slots`].

holders.description: Everyone holding it, at most [`slots`] of them, the one holding it longest first.

waiting.description: Who's waiting for it, next first.

held.description:
This machine's sessions whose requests it holds back until it has room, as its
`config.toml` says (`[leases.<name>]`): they've not asked the others yet.

Lease.description: A lease as it is: who holds it and who's waiting.

until.description:
When it holds the lease until, or when waiting, until when it'd hold it if its turn
came now: in seconds since the Unix epoch.

Holder.description: A session holding or waiting for a lease.

Held.description: A session's request this machine holds back until it has room for the lease.

name.description:
Its name, which is its nick on the server: unique in the organisation ([`check_name`]),
such as `fixer`.

repository.description:
The repository its seat is taken from a checkout of, by name as zirc spells it
([`crate::Message::repo`]), such as `monorepo`.

brief.description: What it does, given to whoever takes it, as zirc.dev's "What it does" says.

triggers.description: What wakes its holder, besides a direct message, which always does.

reports.description:
The kinds of report it takes ([`crate::role_report::Subject`]), as its admins chose
them on zirc.dev's Roles tab.

Definition.description: A role as an organisation's admins define it on zirc.dev.

said.description:
Words that wake it when a person or an integration says them, whatever their case, as
words of their own: `refund` isn't in `refunded`.

reaction.description: The reaction that wakes it when a person gives it to a message, such as `🐛`.

landed.description:
Paths a landing changes to wake it: a file, or a directory for everything under
it; `.` for any landing. As CI says what a landing changed ([`crate::ci::Data`]).

every.description:
How often it wakes by itself, such as `1d` ([`seconds`]): at every whole multiple
of it since 1 January 1970 UTC, so `1d` is each midnight and `6h` is 0, 6, 12 and 18.

at.description: The time of day it wakes at, `HH:MM` in UTC, when `every` is whole days.

day.description: The day of the week it wakes on, `mon` to `sun`, when `every` is `7d`.

Trigger.description:
What wakes a role's holder on its own ([`crate::roles`]), each trigger one of: a state
([`crate::state`]) being said, a time coming round (`every`), words someone says
(`said`), a person's reaction to a message (`reaction`), or a landing that changes some
paths (`landed`).

```toml
state = "master"
level = "broken"

every = "7d"          # at least [`MIN_EVERY`]
day = "mon"           # with 7d alone; Thursdays without it
at = "09:00"          # UTC, when `every` is whole days; midnight without it

said = "refund"       # a person or an integration says it, as words of its own

reaction = "🐛"        # a person's, on a message

landed = ["server", "MODULE.bazel"]   # files, or everything under a directory
```

last.description: Who held it before, for "Last held by" and `zirc role last`.

waiting.description: How many direct messages wait for the next holder.

wakes_on.description:
What wakes it, as people read it ([`Definition::wakes_on`]): said here for readers
that can't run this crate, such as zirc.dev's Roles tab.

woke_today.description: How many times it woke today, UTC: by a direct message, a trigger or a report.

Seat.description: How a role stands: who holds its seat, if anyone, and who did last.

since.description: Since when it held it, or until when it did for the last holder: unix seconds.

session.description: The session's id, as its messages carry it.

name.description: Its short handle ([`crate::Message::name`]), when it has one.

title.description: Its full title, as the agent tool shows it, at most [`MAX_TITLE`] characters.

tool.description: The agent tool it runs in ([`crate::Message::tool`]), when known.

Holder2.description:
A session holding a role, or that held it: its machine, and the session as its card says
it ([`crate::session::SessionCard`]), so its name and tool are read one way.

roles.description: Every role, in the order zirc.dev lists them.

addresses.description:
Each role's webhook address, as the server knows it: by its secret's digest alone.
The server never says them back ([`Listing::without_addresses`]).

version.description: What they're at: anything that changes when they do, a new secret too.

Listing.description:
An organisation's roles, as zirc.dev syncs them to its server: whole each time, with a
version that changes whenever they do.

digest.description: The SHA-256 of its secret, in hex ([`Address::digest_of`]).

Address.description:
A role's webhook address ([`INBOUND_PATH`]) as its server is given it: the SHA-256 of its
secret, in lowercase hex, never the secret, which zirc.dev keeps for the role's admins. A
new secret (Rotate, on zirc.dev) is a new listing, which the server takes at once, and the
old one opens nothing from then on.

listing.description: The roles, as zirc.dev last synced them.

seats.description: Each role's seat, in the same order.

Standing.description:
How an organisation's roles stand, as its server answers at [`PATH`]: each role, and its
seat, in the listing's order.

value.description: At most 120 characters, in zirc-chat's Markdown, so it can be a link.

id.description:
The integration's own name for it: 1–32 of lowercase letters, digits, `_` and `-`,
unique in the card.

who.description: Who apps show it to; [`Who::Members`] when it doesn't say.

confirm.description: What apps ask before sending it, at most 120 characters.

Action.description:
A button. Pressing it reaches the integration that posted the card, which decides
whether the person may.

oneOf.description: The organisation's members: everyone in the channel, as when a button doesn't say.

Anyone in the channel: the same as [`Who::Members`], as only members are in its
channels. Kept because cards say it.
The person the card is about: the owner of its `about` session, or that nick.
The organisation's owners and admins.
The organisation's owners.

Who.description: Who may press a button, as apps show it: the integration decides.

state.description:
How it stands: [`State::Pending`] until it starts, [`State::Cancelled`] when it was
skipped; [`State::Info`] when it doesn't say.

detail.description: At most 32 characters beside it, such as `onto 43cdc6e` or `//web:e2e`.

done.description: How much of it is done, of [`Step::of`]: apps draw a bar and `81 / 214`.

of.description: How much there is to do, such as 214 targets.

secs.description: How many seconds it took, or has taken so far.

Step.description: A step of what a card is about, such as a build's "Build and test".

file.description: The file, as zirc.dev hosts it: an image.

alt.description: What it shows, for a screen reader and where it isn't drawn: at most 120 characters.

results.description: Where its result in this build is, on zirc.dev/test-results.

CiFailed.description: A target that failed in a landing's build.

branch.description: The branch, on the repository's remote.

commit.description: Its head, in full, as CI found it.

CiStackedOn.description: A branch a landing's or try's branch was stacked on ([`Data::stacked_on`]).

such as from `zirc search`.

Where the command runs, which names the organisation on a machine signed in to
several.

operator of.
oneOf.title: TrimRequest

session.description:
The session watching: an agent session working here, or none for the machine's
person.

oneOf.description:
Stream every zirc message from the channels being watched, and overlaps with this
machine's own uncommitted changes as they appear, each with why it concerns
`session`, if it does.
oneOf.title: WatchRequest

days.description: How many days back, today included.

oneOf.description:
How this machine's sessions' watches woke over the last `days` days, and how often
the session acted soon after: answered with [`Response::Wakes`]. Counts only.
oneOf.title: WakesRequest

oneOf.description:
Let wakes through again at once, the circuit breaker on them being open, and count
afresh: answered with [`Response::Wakes`].
oneOf.title: WakesResumeRequest

landing.description:
For a landing (`//ops:land`), which claims the task: the one the session is on,
else the one it finished last, if in the last [`LANDING_CLAIMS`] seconds and no
landing claimed it yet, since sessions often post `done:` before they land. A task
an intent started, with no `taking:`, ends with its landing.

oneOf.description:
The task `session` is on, the id zircd gave it when it posted `taking:` or, on none,
stated an intent ([`zirc_proto::Message::task`]): answered with [`Response::Task`].
oneOf.title: TaskRequest

states.description: The states it waits on changing.

reactions.description:
The reactions it waits for, such as 👀: the machine's person giving one to a
message wakes the session ([`Why::ReactionAwaited`]), once a message, however
often it's given. Each lasts a day from when it was said or last woke the session.

drop.description: Stop waiting for `reactions`, rather than start.

oneOf.description:
Note that `session` waits on each of `on`, another session, a branch or a build by its
number, so CI's landing line naming it wakes the session ([`Why::Awaited`]) until it
lands, fails or conflicts, or for three hours; and on each of `states` changing, so
the first state said of it at another level wakes it ([`Why::StateChanged`]), once.
With nothing in either, it says what the session waits on. Answered with
[`Response::Awaits`].
oneOf.title: WaitForRequest

session.description: The session whose branch is stacked.

tip.description: That branch's head as the session built on it.

gone.description: Whether origin, asked as the stack was said, no longer has `branch`.

oneOf.description:
Note that `session`'s branch is stacked on `branch`, another session's not yet
landed, whose head was `tip` as the session built on it: CI's line saying it landed
wakes the session ([`Why::BranchLanded`]), as does a push that moves it
([`Why::Landing`]), and the stack is kept, with `tip`, for the rebase onto the default
branch that follows. With `drop`, forget the stack on `branch`; with no `branch`, only
say the session's stacks. With `gone`, origin answered just now that it has no such
branch any more. Answered with [`Response::Stacks`].
oneOf.title: StackRequest

oneOf.description: Stop zircd, after answering.
oneOf.title: StopRequest

oneOf.description:
Start zircd again from its binary, after answering, as after an update: watches are
told [`RESTARTING`] and watch again once it's back.
oneOf.title: RestartRequest

seconds.description:
How long to hold it once it's theirs: [`crate::leases::DEFAULT_SECONDS`] unless
said, at most [`crate::leases::MAX_SECONDS`].

pid.description:
The asking `zirc` command's process id: zircd gives the lease back once nothing
heavy has run for a while under whoever ran it, such as the session's agent.

wait.description:
Whether the asking command waits until the lease is the session's (`zirc lease
--wait`): while `pid` runs, it says so itself, so the session's watch isn't told.

oneOf.description:
Ask for the lease `name` for `session` ([`crate::leases`]), or, holding it, hold it
for `seconds` from now: while others wait, no further than [`crate::leases::renewal`]
allows, past which it's asked for again behind them. Answered with
[`Response::Leases`] holding that lease.
oneOf.title: LeaseRequest

session.description: The session holding or waiting for it.

oneOf.description:
Give back the lease `name`, or stop waiting for it, as `session`. Answered with
[`Response::Leases`] holding that lease.
oneOf.title: LeaseReleaseRequest

oneOf.description: Every lease held or waited for. Answered with [`Response::Leases`].
oneOf.title: LeasesRequest

repo.description: The repository of the checkout it's taken in, as zirc spells it.

oneOf.description:
Take role `role`'s one seat ([`zirc_proto::roles`]) for `session`, in a checkout of
`repo`, its lease asked for and held while the session's watch lives. Refused when
another session holds it, or the role's repository isn't `repo`. Answered with
[`Response::RoleTaken`].
oneOf.title: RoleTakeRequest

oneOf.description: Leave the role `session` holds. Answered with [`Response::Done`].
oneOf.title: RoleLeaveRequest

reply_to.description: The message it answers, by id.

oneOf.description:
Say `text` as the role `session` holds: to `to` directly, answering `reply_to`, or
without `to` in the agents' room. Answered with [`Response::Done`].
oneOf.title: RoleSayRequest

oneOf.description:
How the organisation's roles stand, from its server. Answered with
[`Response::RoleStanding`].
oneOf.title: RoleStandingRequest

oneOf.description: The answer to [`Request::Status`].
oneOf.title: StatusResponse

repos.description: The repositories being watched, sorted by path.

oneOf.description: The answer to [`Request::RepoList`], and to adding or removing one.
oneOf.title: ReposResponse

oneOf.description: Done, with nothing to say.
oneOf.title: DoneResponse

link.description:
The post's own link, which opens it in every app
([`zirc_proto::link::conversation_link`]), once the server's echo gave its id.

oneOf.description: The channel a post, join or leave was about.
oneOf.title: ChannelResponse

channels.description: Each joined channel's working sets, sorted by channel.

oneOf.description: The answer to [`Request::Who`].
oneOf.title: WhoResponse

stacks.description: The branches it's stacked on, oldest first.

oneOf.description: A session's stacks: the answer to [`Request::Stack`].
oneOf.title: StacksResponse

on.description: Sessions, branches and builds by their number.

oneOf.description: What a session waits on: the answer to [`Request::WaitFor`].
oneOf.title: AwaitsResponse

oneOf.description: The answer to [`Request::Read`].
oneOf.title: MessagesResponse

targets.description: The nicks of the people and machines each conversation is with.

oneOf.description: The answer to [`Request::Conversations`].
oneOf.title: ConversationsResponse

oneOf.description: One message, while watching.
oneOf.title: DeliveryResponse

oneOf.description: While watching: this machine's owner answered a session's request.
oneOf.title: AnsweredResponse

oneOf.description: While watching: a message sent to this machine's nick rather than to a channel.
oneOf.title: DirectResponse

oneOf.description: While watching: someone reacted to a message, or took a reaction back.
oneOf.title: ReactionResponse

gone.description: Those seen live since zircd started that no longer are, sorted.

oneOf.description: The answer to [`Request::LiveSessions`].
oneOf.title: LiveSessionsResponse

sessions.description: Each session given a name, a title or a link here.

oneOf.description: The answer to [`Request::LocalSessions`], by session.
oneOf.title: LocalSessionsResponse

counts.description: A count for each day and reason a watch woke.

breaker.description: The circuit breaker on wakes, from a zircd that has one.

oneOf.description: The answer to [`Request::Wakes`], oldest day first.
oneOf.title: WakesResponse

task.description: The task's id, while the session is on one.

oneOf.description: The answer to [`Request::Task`].
oneOf.title: TaskResponse

id.description: The request's id, which its answer names.

taken.description:
The answer taken at once, the session's own recommendation, on a machine set to
take them (`accept_recommended`): the session acts on it now, and hears on its
watch if its person later says otherwise.

oneOf.description: The answer to [`Request::AskOwner`].
oneOf.title: RequestedResponse

channels.description: The channels it was posted to.

oneOf.description: The answer to [`Request::Decide`].
oneOf.title: DecidedResponse

oneOf.description:
The answer to [`Request::Note`], and to a [`Request::Post`] addressed to one agent
session, which goes to it as a note.
oneOf.title: NotedResponse

text.description: The line, as it's said in the agents' room.

said.description: Whether this request said it: not when the other side had said the same already.

oneOf.description: The answer to [`Request::Settle`].
oneOf.title: SettledResponse

id.description: The query's id, which its answers name.

to.description:
The machines it went to: this one's own nick among them when it was for its
own sessions.

oneOf.description: The answer to [`Request::Ask`].
oneOf.title: AskedResponse

queries.description: Who may query this machine's agents.

colleagues_kept_out.description:
Whether the organisation keeps other members' agents out whatever this machine
says, so `anyone` takes only its owner's own (`zirc_proto::colleagues`).

oneOf.description: The answer to [`Request::Queries`].
oneOf.title: QueriesResponse

oneOf.description: While watching: someone else started changing paths this machine has changed too.
oneOf.title: OverlapResponse

oneOf.description: While watching: two worktrees on this machine started changing the same paths.
oneOf.title: LocalOverlapResponse

oneOf.description: The answer to [`Request::Unseal`]: the part's value.
oneOf.title: UnsealedResponse

oneOf.description: While watching: a push changes the same lines as a worktree on this machine.
oneOf.title: ConflictResponse

oneOf.description: The answer to [`Request::Lease`], [`Request::LeaseRelease`] and [`Request::Leases`].
oneOf.title: LeasesResponse

oneOf.description:
The answer to [`Request::RoleTake`]: the role, whose brief its holder is given, and
how it stood when taken, its last holder among it.
oneOf.title: RoleTakenResponse

oneOf.description: The answer to [`Request::RoleStanding`].
oneOf.title: RoleStandingResponse

message.description: Why, for a person to read.

oneOf.description: The request failed.
oneOf.title: ErrorResponse

id.description:
Unique within its sender: a later card with the same id from the same nick replaces
it. 1–64 of letters, digits and `._:/-`, such as `monorepo/889`.

state.description: Its colour and icon; [`State::Info`] when it doesn't say.

about.description:
The agent session or nick it concerns, such as the session a landing is for. A
[`Who::About`] button is for its owner.

fields.description: At most 8, shown as label and value.

links.description: At most 4, shown under the fields.

steps.description:
At most 10, in order: what it's doing and has done, such as a build's phases. Apps
draw them under the fields, and fold them into one line once the card is done.

note.description: One line under it all, such as who pressed what and how it went, or an error.

image.description:
A picture under its title, such as a preview deploy's screenshot: a file zirc.dev
hosts, uploaded as a shared one is. Apps draw it only from zirc.dev, as they draw a
shared file, never loading another address.

subject.description: What the landing is about: its head commit's subject, which apps show as its headline.

session.description: The session that queued it, whom the text names.

machine.description:
The nick of the machine [`Data::session`] runs on: a session's id is unique only on
its machine, so the machine and the session together say whose landing it is.

commit.description: The full id of the commit the text names.

failed.description: The targets that failed, each with where its result is.

cause.description:
On a landing that didn't land: why, one of [`CAUSES`], for counting what stops
landings.

task.description:
The task the landing finishes or is part of ([`crate::Message::task`]): the one its
session is on or just finished, else one of the landing's own, from its zircd.

reverts.description:
Full ids of the commits on the default branch the landing undoes, from its commits'
`Reverts:` trailers.

fixes.description:
What the landing repairs, from its commits' `Fixes:` trailers: full ids of commits on
the default branch, or CI builds as `build N`.

changed.description:
On a landing that passed: the paths it changed, from the repository's root, for what
follows landings by where they land (a role's `landed` trigger). Where it changed
many files in a directory, CI may name the directory, ending in `/`, in their place.

deploys.description:
On a deploy's event: every app the landing deploys to production, of every kind, so a
wait for the landing to be deployed ends once all of them are, not on the first.

deployed.description: On a deploy's event: the apps this event says were deployed.

steps.description: A landing's steps as they stand ([`crate::card::Step`]): its card shows them.

try.description:
A try (`//ops:land --try`): the branch tested as its landing would be, rebased onto
the default branch, and never landed, on every event of its build. Its end, passed, is
at `info`, never `passed`, which counts as landed.

test.description:
Whether it's a test failure a person sent to see their agent wake (`zirc ci
test-failure`): a real run that failed on purpose, so there's nothing to fix.

stacked_on.description:
The branches, still to land, whose commits the branch held as CI found it: what it was
tested on, for a try, and why it failed, for a landing, which CI refuses then, as it
would land their commits as its own.

CiData.description:
What a landing's or deploy's event carries (`ops/say.sh`), each field left out when CI
doesn't know it. Every event of one landing's build has the same [`Data::landing`], so the
apps show them as one landing that updates.
